newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dlr should firm to 1.80-2.00 dmk - Germany's VDMA.
newsitem.headline: Dlr should firm to 1.80-2.00 dmk - Germany's VDMA.

text.p: A dollar exchange rate of 1.80 to two marks would be more appropriate than the current rate of around 1.71 marks, the head of Germany's machine and plant construction industry association VDMA said on Thursday.

Taking into account real purchasing power levels in the U.S. and Germany and the fundamental strengthening of the U.S. economy in the last five to seven years, the dollar should be firmer than it is now, VDMA president Michael Rogowski told a news conference.
"I'd like to say that a dollar/mark rate of 1.80 to two marks would be more correct than at 1.60 to 1.70 marks," Rogowski said.

He added that the recent appreciation of the dollar, the British pound and the Italian lira against the mark had helped German exporters and improved prospects for an upturn in the German engineering industry this year.
A weaker mark helps boost German exports by making the country's products less expensive abroad.
The German machine and plant construction sector employs about 940,000 people and represents about 5,500 companies.
